name: Future Value of a Daily Habit
description: Shows what a small daily expense would grow to if invested instead each year.
notes: 5 a day invested at 7 % for 30 years grows to about 172,000.

name: Cost of Delaying Investment
description: Gives how much less a lump sum grows to if it is invested d years later.
notes: Five years' delay on 10,000 at 7 % costs about 22,000 by year 30.

name: Real Hourly Wage
description: Divides take-home pay minus the costs of working by all the hours the job really takes (from Your Money or Your Life).
notes: Useful to judge purchases in hours of life.

name: Annual Salary from an Hourly Rate
description: Converts an hourly rate to yearly pay.
notes: 25 an hour full time is 52,000 a year.

name: Hourly Rate from an Annual Salary
description: Converts a yearly salary to an hourly rate.
notes: A useful comparison when overtime or contract work is on offer.

name: Stacked Discounts
description: Applies two percentage discounts one after the other.
notes: 30 % off and then 20 % off is 44 % off in total, not 50 %.

name: Effective Discount of "Buy X Get Y Free"
description: Gives the equivalent percentage discount of a buy-x-get-y-free offer.
notes: "Buy 2 get 1 free" is a 33.3 % discount, not 50 %.

name: Bill Split with Tip
description: Divides a bill plus tip equally among a group.
notes: Round up to a convenient amount if paying cash.

name: Currency Conversion after Fee
description: Converts money at a quoted rate and deducts the provider's fee or spread.
notes: Card and airport rates often hide 2–5 % in the spread.

name: Car Lease Monthly Payment
description: Gives a lease payment as the depreciation charge plus the finance charge (money factor times the sum of cost and residual).

name: Money Factor to APR
description: Converts a lease money factor to an approximate annual percentage rate.
notes: A money factor of 0.0025 is about 6 % APR.

name: Credit Utilisation Ratio
description: Divides revolving balances by credit limits; a major factor in credit scores.
notes: Keeping it below about 30 % (ideally under 10 %) helps scores.

name: Emergency Fund Target
description: Gives the cash reserve for a chosen number of months of essential spending.
notes: Three to six months is the usual advice; more for irregular incomes.

name: Savings Rate
description: Gives the share of take-home income that is saved.
notes: The single biggest driver of how soon financial independence is reached.

name: Price per Unit Comparison (Savings of the Bigger Pack)
description: Compares unit prices and gives how much cheaper per unit the second pack is.
notes: Negative means the "bigger" pack is actually more expensive per unit.
